quizName: DMV Practice Test #14 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: What increases fatigue while riding?

options.text: Starting a ride late in the day.

questions.explanation: To reduce fatigue, dress to protect yourself from wind and rain. Ride no more than six hours per day. Stop for a break at least every two hours. Do not use artificial stimulants, as extreme fatigue can occur when they wear off.

questions.question: When turning left, what should you do?

options.text: Press both handgrips at the same time.

questions.explanation: To turn left, press the left handgrip. Pressing the handgrip in the direction you want to turn makes the motorcycle lean the right way.

questions.question: How can you prevent other vehicles from sharing your lane?

options.text: Ride in the middle of your lane.
Ride in the left portion of your lane.
Ride in the right portion of your lane.
Swerve from side to side in your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the middle of your lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane. This discourages other drivers from trying to share your space.

questions.question: Which sign is rectangular in shape?
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs like speed limits are rectangular with white background and black lettering. You must follow the rules on these signs.

questions.question: What does a linked braking system do?

options.text: Connects the front and rear brakes so both brakes apply when either lever is used.
Connects the front brake to the gear shifter, applying the brake when you downshift.
Connects the rear brake to a foot control.
Connects the rear brake to a handlebar switch.

questions.correctAnswerText: Connects the front and rear brakes so both brakes apply when either lever is used.
questions.explanation: A linked braking system connects the front and rear brakes. Using either brake lever applies pressure to both brakes. Check your owner's manual for details about your motorcycle's braking system.

questions.question: Why should you not ride too far right with a sidecar or three-wheeled motorcycle?

options.text: Other drivers may not see you.
You will not be able to pass other vehicles as easily.
Other drivers may try to share your lane.
You may run off the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may run off the road.
questions.explanation: A sidecar sits on the right side. Riding too far right can cause the sidecar to leave the road. On a three-wheeled motorcycle, the rear right wheel could run off the road if you ride too close to the right edge.

questions.question: How should you apply the front brake?

options.text: Squeeze the lever firmly and increase pressure smoothly.
Grab the brake with only two fingers.
Press down on the brake lever with your foot.

questions.correctAnswerText: Squeeze the lever firmly and increase pressure smoothly.
questions.explanation: Squeeze the brake lever with all four fingers. Apply pressure firmly and smoothly, increasing force gradually.

questions.question: What should you do when riding at night?

options.text: Use the headlights of vehicles ahead to see farther.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the headlights of vehicles ahead to see farther.
questions.explanation: At night, reduce your speed and increase your following distance. Use the headlights of vehicles ahead to see farther down the road. Be flexible with your lane position when riding at night.

questions.question: What following distance should you normally maintain?
questions.explanation: Under normal conditions, stay at least two seconds behind the vehicle ahead of you. Increase this distance when conditions are poor.

questions.question: Which is not a good safety tip?

options.text: Slow to a safe speed before turning.
When turning, lean in the direction you wish to go.
Avoid dragging your feet on the roadway.

questions.explanation: Slow down before turning and lean in the direction of the turn. Do not drag your feet on the road, as they could catch on something and cause you to lose control. Always watch for other traffic.

questions.question: Motorcycles are hard to see at night. What should a motorcycle rider do about this?

options.text: Slow down when riding at night.
Honk their horn repeatedly when riding at night.
Ride directly in front of another vehicle so the headlights show them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down when riding at night.
questions.explanation: Safe night riding includes slowing down, staying farther from the car ahead, using another car's headlights to see the road, using your high beam (unless near other vehicles), and changing your lane position as needed.

questions.question: To work well, a face shield should NOT:
questions.explanation: A good face shield should be scratch-free, block impacts, let you see to the sides, attach securely, and allow air to flow. An airtight shield causes fogging and makes it hard to see.

questions.question: When you are about to pass another vehicle on the left, which part of your lane should you ride in?
questions.explanation: Ride in the left portion of your lane before passing. This helps you see the road ahead better and makes oncoming traffic see you.

questions.question: When riding at night, you should do all of these EXCEPT:

options.text: Use the headlights of vehicles ahead to help you see.
Ride only in the left portion of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride only in the left portion of your lane.
questions.explanation: Use your high beam (unless near other vehicles), use other vehicles' headlights to help you see, and wear reflective gear. Change your lane position as needed to see better, be seen, and stay safe.

questions.question: When a group of riders leaves a highway, what formation should they use?
questions.explanation: Groups usually ride staggered, but should switch to single-file when turning, taking curves, or entering or leaving a highway.

questions.question: When you are about to pass another vehicle on the left, you should ride in:

options.text: The left side of the lane.
The right side of the lane.
Either the right or center portions of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The left side of the lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the left side of your lane before passing. This position gives you the best view of the road ahead.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black letters or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: If you need to stop quickly while in a curve, you should:

options.text: Straighten the bike, square the handlebars, and stop.
Apply both brakes hard while still leaning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Straighten the bike, square the handlebars, and stop.
questions.explanation: Straighten and square the handlebars first, then stop. If you cannot straighten the bike, brake smoothly and slowly. Reduce your lean angle and increase brake pressure as you slow down.

questions.question: ______ means another driver definitely sees you.
questions.explanation: Nothing guarantees that a driver sees you. Always assume that any vehicle that could enter your path will do so.

questions.question: When it is raining, what is usually the best thing to do?

options.text: Ride in the center of the lane.
Stop on the side of the road until the rain stops.
Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: Wet pavement is slippery, especially when rain first starts. Oil from cars still sits on the road. Ride in the tire tracks left by cars. The left track is often the safest choice.

questions.question: Where do most motorcycle crashes happen?
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen on trips shorter than five miles at speeds under 30 mph.

questions.question: Without a helmet, a motorcycle rider is ________ more likely to suffer a critical head injury in a crash.
questions.explanation: Without a helmet, a rider is five times more likely to suffer a critical head injury in a crash.

questions.question: What is the best way to protect yourself while riding?

options.text: Keep space between your motorcycle and other vehicles

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep space between your motorcycle and other vehicles
questions.explanation: The best protection against crashes is keeping distance from other vehicles. This gives you time to react if another driver makes a mistake. Wearing proper protective gear is also important.

questions.question: What percentage of motorcycle-car crashes are caused by the car driver failing to yield the right-of-way?
questions.explanation: More than half of motorcycle-car crashes happen because the car driver fails to yield the right-of-way to the rider.

questions.question: Under ideal riding conditions, what is the minimum following distance you should maintain?
questions.explanation: In normal conditions, keep at least two seconds of distance between you and the vehicle ahead. Increase this distance if conditions are not ideal.
